cards.title: Standard Shopping structures: top-sellers split, feeder, and labelizer
cards.summary: Three in-market Shopping structures plus when each is (and isn't) worth the complexity.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to organize standard Shopping campaigns for a store's catalog.

cards.title: Run Search campaigns only for the right cases; use STAGs and front-load negatives
cards.summary: Search is secondary for most ecom, but essential with B2B — structure with topic ad groups and aggressive early negative-keyword policing.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in Search and how to police it for a store.

cards.title: Treat landing-page testing as the biggest Search lever
cards.summary: A/B test landing pages within ad groups over 30-60 days to raise conversion rate and unlock higher bids.
cards.use_when: Running acquisition on Google and looking to increase conversion rate and winning auctions.

cards.title: Fix seven common Google Ads account hygiene mistakes
cards.summary: Audit and correct frequent account-level setup errors that waste budget or distort attribution.
cards.use_when: Auditing an ecommerce Google Ads account for structural errors before scaling.

cards.title: Google Ads bidding: expansive vs restrictive strategies
cards.summary: Choose between expansive (Max Conversions/Max Conversion Value) and restrictive (tROAS/tCPA) bidding based on whether you need to test new audiences for scale or protect efficiency.
cards.use_when: Deciding on the account-level bidding strategy for a Google Search, Shopping or PMax campaign and diagnosing whether the current strategy is starving the campaign of new-audience tests.

cards.title: Prefer value-based bidding for ecommerce over lowest-CPA bidding
cards.summary: In ecommerce, optimising for Max Conversions pushes budget to the cheapest product; Max Conversion Value optimises towards margin mix instead.
cards.use_when: Setting or auditing the bidding objective for an ecommerce Google Ads account with a wide price range across products.

cards.title: Detect and stop the tROAS death spiral
cards.summary: A tROAS target that stops being met shrinks targeting, reduces spend, starves the model of conversion data and accelerates decline — pull the target back aggressively and early.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a Google Ads account where spend and conversions are gradually trailing off over weeks and campaigns appear to be dying.

cards.title: Merge campaign learnings with portfolio bidding strategies
cards.summary: Portfolio bid strategies let segmented campaigns share learning and let you apply max/min CPC caps on top of value-based bidding.
cards.use_when: You need tight campaign segmentation for reporting or structure but individual campaigns are too data-starved to learn well, or you want to cap expensive clicks in a high-CPC niche.

cards.title: Change Google Ads budgets and strategies slowly, downward faster than upward
cards.summary: Increase Google budgets in roughly 20% increments; reductions can be faster, but large overnight increases or bidding changes cause instability.
cards.use_when: Scaling or cutting spend on a Google Ads campaign and deciding how large a single change to make.

cards.title: Optimise Google Merchant Center titles from search term data
cards.summary: Product feed titles are the main lever for Shopping and PMax placement; build them from historically converting search terms rather than default product names.
cards.use_when: Improving Shopping or PMax performance by rewriting product feed titles, or auditing a feed where default variant names are being used.

cards.title: Spin variant listings to cover multiple keyword pools
cards.summary: When a product has multiple variants, each variant generates its own Shopping listing — use separate titles and creative per variant to target different keyword pools and audiences.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a multi-variant product (sizes, formats, pack sizes) in Google Shopping or PMax and looking to expand reach without duplicating landing pages.

cards.title: Fix feed image aspect ratios and build contrast for click-through
cards.summary: Shopping images occupy most of the listing real estate, so match the platform's required aspect ratio and design for contrast against competing listings — not for maximum CTR on the wrong audience.
cards.use_when: Auditing product feed imagery for a Shopping or PMax campaign where CTR is weak or images are being auto-cropped.

cards.title: Set up separate feeds per currency for international Shopping
cards.summary: Running multiple regions through a single-currency feed forces live currency conversion on the listing, which suppresses CTR and conversion.
cards.use_when: Selling to customers in more than one currency via Google Shopping and reviewing the feed structure.

cards.title: Sequence the 90-day Google Ads improvement rollout
cards.summary: Implement Google Ads fixes in a defined order: tracking, structure map, PMax checks, waste removal, assets, then feed changes slowly.
cards.use_when: Planning an account-wide Google Ads overhaul or onboarding a new ecommerce account with multiple issues to fix.

cards.title: Run a 5-minute business-level diagnostic before touching Google Ads
cards.summary: Before troubleshooting Google, verify cross-channel spend mix, decompose the revenue equation, separate attributed from true business KPIs, and rule out seasonality.
cards.use_when: Revenue or efficiency has dipped and you are deciding whether the problem is even a Google Ads problem before diving into the account.

cards.title: Complete three pre-checks before any Google Ads diagnosis
cards.summary: Check change history, extend the time horizon, and use conversions-by-conversion-time before concluding performance has genuinely declined.
cards.use_when: Starting an account diagnostic or about to make changes after noticed a performance dip.

cards.title: Drill from account to campaign to ad group to find the inflection point
cards.summary: Troubleshoot Google Ads by sorting campaigns by spend, plotting metrics on 90–180 day weekly views, and locating the exact date performance changed — then descend to the responsible campaign and ad group.
cards.use_when: A confirmed Google Ads performance decline needs to be traced to a specific campaign type, campaign and ad group.

cards.title: Diagnose PMax failures: warm/cold drift, disapprovals, tROAS narrowing, product bloat
cards.summary: PMax campaigns fail in four recurring ways — audience drift, feed disapprovals, tROAS-driven audience narrowing, and product/SKU churn resetting learning.
cards.use_when: Troubleshooting a declining Performance Max campaign in an ecommerce account.

cards.title: Diagnose Search campaign failures: search terms, auctions, tROAS, display leakage
cards.summary: Search campaign declines typically trace to changed search term spend allocation, new auction competition, raised tROAS or unintended display spend.
cards.use_when: Troubleshooting a declining Google Search campaign where volume or efficiency has dropped.

cards.title: Diagnose Shopping campaign failures through the feed first
cards.summary: Shopping failures closely mirror PMax mechanics minus audience drift; the dominant causes are feed and product availability issues.
cards.use_when: Troubleshooting a declining Google Shopping campaign in an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Decompose campaign KPIs via submetric formulas for root cause analysis
cards.summary: Every campaign metric is a product of underlying metrics; drilling into the right submetric locates the true root cause instead of a symptom.
cards.use_when: Investigating why a specific campaign's revenue, ROAS, CPA or conversion volume moved, in order to find the actual root cause.

cards.title: Use revenue equation to route ecommerce diagnosis
cards.summary: Revenue = conversion rate × AOV × sessions; identifying which lever moved tells you whether to look at the website, a traffic source, or product mix.
cards.use_when: A top-line revenue decline needs to be attributed to a store-side or media-side cause before choosing a fix.

cards.title: Google Ads Diagnostic Tree: Top-Down Root Cause Analysis
cards.summary: A top-down order of investigation for diagnosing Google Ads performance declines, from business level down to the submetric.
cards.use_when: Paid search or Shopping performance has dipped and you must decide whether to act, what to change, and in what order before touching the account.

cards.title: Diagnosing Rising CPC: Three Causes and When It Actually Matters
cards.summary: CPC is treated as a vanity metric; diagnose quality score, new auction entrants, and premium auction entry before reacting.
cards.use_when: Cost per click has risen in Google Ads, Meta or TikTok and you need to decide whether it signals a real problem for store acquisition cost.

cards.title: Diagnosing Falling Conversion Rate: Tracking, Landing Page, Audience, Learning, Offer
cards.summary: A five-step check for conversion-rate declines, ordered from tracking errors to offer changes, that applies to platform and storefront conversion alike.
cards.use_when: Ad platform conversion rate or site conversion rate has dropped and you need to separate measurement artefacts from real storefront problems before rebuilding anything.

cards.title: Diagnosing Volume Declines: Impressions, Impression Share and CTR
cards.summary: When efficiency holds but volume falls, trace it to clicks, then to impressions lost to budget versus bid, then to CTR.
cards.use_when: Google Ads revenue or spend has fallen while CPA is stable, and you need to decide whether to raise budget, raise bids, or change creative.

cards.title: Competitor Price Monitoring to Pull Products Before Margin Erosion
cards.summary: A real-time competitor price script that de-prioritises or pulls products from Shopping rather than matching discounts to zero margin.
cards.use_when: Shopping CTR or product-level ROAS drops on specific SKUs and you suspect a competitor has discounted the identical product.

cards.title: Fix Before Rebuild: Avoiding the Learning-Phase Death Spiral
cards.summary: Default to targeted fixes over rebuilds because every rebuild triggers a learning reset that can deepen the decline.
cards.use_when: A Google Ads account is underperforming and you are considering restructuring campaigns or the account to fix it.

cards.title: Bundling Versus Isolating Fixes: Choosing Based on Severity
cards.summary: Decide whether to apply one fix at a time for learning, or many at once to rescue a severe decline.
cards.use_when: A storefront or paid media metric has dropped and you are deciding how many changes to ship in the same iteration.

cards.title: Pre-Investigation Checks Before Touching Any Ad Account
cards.summary: Three checks — change history, attribution latency, cross-channel sanity — that should precede any in-platform action.
cards.use_when: A stakeholder reports a performance problem in Google Ads and you are tempted to adjust settings immediately.

cards.title: Read CAC Only Against Gross Profit, Not in Isolation
cards.summary: CAC is meaningless without context; judge it against gross profit per first order and over cohort life.
cards.use_when: Evaluating paid acquisition performance or deciding whether you can afford to scale spend in your store.

cards.title: Question Any LTV:CAC Number: Horizon and Observed vs Modeled
cards.summary: When a brand touts an LTV/LTGP-to-CAC ratio, ask what time horizon it's measured on and how much is observed vs modeled.
cards.use_when: Reviewing your own or a partner's unit economics before scaling spend, raising, or benchmarking against competitors.

cards.title: Don't Be Fooled by Annualized ARR from One Strong Month
cards.summary: ARR is usually one month times twelve, so a single exceptional month distorts the picture.
cards.use_when: Assessing your store's revenue trajectory or a competitor/partner's reported recurring revenue.

cards.title: Distinguish Cash-Flow-Positive from Genuinely Profitable
cards.summary: Financing that pre-pays acquisition cost can make a brand look cash-flow-positive while true profitability is unchanged.
cards.use_when: Interpreting 'cash flow positive' claims about your store or a partner's business when deciding to scale or invest.

cards.title: Steer Awareness-Stage Traffic to the Matching Destination
cards.summary: Match ad-to-landing-page by stage of awareness: educate cold traffic, be congruent for problem/solution traffic, and send bottom-funnel to product pages.
cards.use_when: Deciding where each ad or campaign should link in your store's acquisition funnel.

cards.title: Clone the Winning Ad Script and Swap Only the Persona
cards.summary: Use one proven script structure with a fixed mechanism and offer, changing only the persona to scale creative output fast.
cards.use_when: Producing ad creative at volume for your store when you have one or more proven winning angles.

cards.title: The Clock/Timeline Ad Script Structure
cards.summary: A proven long-form ad format walks day-by-day transformation, naming a specific compound at each checkpoint and painting scenes instead of claiming outcomes.
cards.use_when: Writing or briefing long-form video ad scripts for a supplement or consumable product.

cards.title: Ladder Product Pricing to a Middle Option
cards.summary: Use a high price anchor (e.g. a premium bundle) to make the middle tier look reasonable and affordable.
cards.use_when: Structuring your store's product tiers, bundles, or subscription plan options.

cards.title: Test Quarterly Plans for CAC Arbitrage, Don't Wholesale Switch
cards.summary: A quarterly subscription default can raise AOV, but only adopt it if CAC doesn't rise proportionally — test it separately.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to shift your store's default checkout from monthly to quarterly (or another longer commitment).

cards.title: Offer-Stack the First Purchase (and Future Milestones)
cards.summary: Attach physical bonuses to the first order and additional freebies at future months to lift first-purchase value and retention.
cards.use_when: Designing PDPs, cart, and first-order offers for a consumable/CPG product.

cards.title: Fix Social-Proof and Detail Discrepancies Before They Become Compliance Risk
cards.summary: Inconsistent claim numbers and ingredient counts across ads are a red flag, especially for regulated or public brands.
cards.use_when: Auditing your store's ad library and marketing copy for consistency and compliance.

cards.title: Persona-Specific Landing Pages Beat a Catch-All Homepage
cards.summary: Build a dedicated landing page for every winning persona/angle instead of routing diverse traffic to a homepage.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to build persona landing pages and where to send varied acquisition traffic.

cards.title: Make Your Value Props Actually Unique
cards.summary: Trust signals everyone can replicate (badges, generic reviews) carry little upside; profit lies in differently demonstrable proof.
cards.use_when: Differentiating your store's PDP or landing page trust and value proposition.

cards.title: Turn Escalating Costs into Decaying Margins via Equity Deals
cards.summary: Partnership costs structured as equity royalties fall as a percentage of revenue, opening margin as you scale.
cards.use_when: Structuring long-term partner, creator, or affiliate deals for your store.

cards.title: Treat Operating Cost as a Percentage That Should Fall with Scale
cards.summary: Direct-to-consumer model economics come from operating costs shrinking as a share of revenue as you scale.
cards.use_when: Reviewing your store's P&L structure and forecasting when margin should open up.

cards.title: Place Where Your Audience's Awareness Sits
cards.summary: The awareness-stage mix of your creative should skew toward problem and solution aware, not product/most aware.
cards.use_when: Planning your store's ad content mix across awareness stages.

cards.title: Increase First-Order AOV to Fund Higher CPA
cards.summary: Shift revenue earlier in the customer relationship by raising first-purchase AOV or defaulting to subscription, so you can afford to spend harder on acquisition without inflating CAC proportionally.
cards.use_when: Repricing offers, designing bundles, or deciding whether to push paid acquisition harder on product selection, PDP or bundle strategy.

cards.title: Clone a Winning Ad Script Across Personas
cards.summary: Find one winning ad script structure, then multiply creative volume by rerunning the same skeleton against many different personas and audiences.
cards.use_when: Scaling acquisition creative volume after identifying at least one ad that reliably converts on your store.

cards.title: Route Persona Ads to Matching Landing Pages
cards.summary: If you change the persona in the ad, make sure the landing page speaks to that same persona — mismatched messaging wastes the targeting.
cards.use_when: Building or updating landing pages and PDPs to match acquisition creative targeting different customer segments.

cards.title: Sell the Mechanism, Not the Benefit
cards.summary: Lead copy and scripts with the unique mechanism behind the result rather than restating the end benefit everyone claims.
cards.use_when: Writing ad scripts, PDP copy or landing pages where differentiation from competing products is weak.

cards.title: Equity Ambassador Deals Instead of Per-Post Fees
cards.summary: Pay long-term partners in equity rather than per-post fees so the cost becomes a smaller percentage of revenue as growth compounds.
cards.use_when: Structuring long-term brand ambassador or influencer partnerships where the relationship will be ongoing and revenue is expected to grow.

cards.title: Do Not Copy IM8's Aggressive Payback Window
cards.summary: IM8's long CAC payback and negative contribution to fund acquisition are enabled by roughly a billion dollars in funding and are not transferable to normal brands.
cards.use_when: Deciding how long an acceptable customer-acquisition payback window can be for your store's cash position.

cards.title: Watch Cohort Maturity Before Judging Acquisition Profitability
cards.summary: Newer cohorts are not yet mature, so read acquisition profit and early-cohort metrics with caution and reconcile them later as cohorts season.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether your paid acquisition is actually profitable when the most recent customer cohorts are still too young to have full lifetime data.

cards.title: Explain the real reason behind small ecommerce requests
cards.summary: Test clear, truthful reasons in opt-in, survey and review-request copy instead of relying on a magic word.
cards.use_when: Writing microcopy for email capture, ask-a-question forms, add-to-cart nudges, or any request where a small yes (email opt-in, review request, survey) is being asked and you want to lift response rate.

cards.title: Sell the Expensive Item First Using Perceptual Contrast
cards.summary: Because shoppers judge price relative to what they just saw, present the costly item before add-ons so accessories look cheap—and never present cheap before expensive.
cards.use_when: Merchandising product pages, bundles, kits or in-store order when designing which item to feature first and how to sequence recommendations and add-on suggestions.

cards.title: Convert Vulnerability into Capability with Reciprocation
cards.summary: Giving a small unsolicited gift or free value before making a request creates a felt obligation that outweighs dislike of the requester and can double compliance.
cards.use_when: Designing lead magnets, free samples, gated-content offers, free tools or trial programs, and deciding whether to give value before asking for the email, purchase or upgrade.

cards.title: Design Free-Sample and Gift Programs as Reciprocation Triggers
cards.summary: Pre-purchase gifting (samples, free shipping credits, content) works as an obligation mechanism when delivered before the request and made non-returnable, not as a discount.
cards.use_when: Structuring a free-sample, sampling-kit, free-shipping threshold or loyalty gift program and deciding what to give, when, and what request to pair it with.

cards.title: Use Price as a Quality Signal Without Deceiving Buyers
cards.summary: Time-pressured or self-doubting shoppers use price as a proxy for quality, so a low-quality listing can be repositioned upward—but the source's own example is a misread price, and outright price deception is risky.
cards.use_when: Repricing a stalled SKU, deciding premium positioning for an unknown-category product, or diagnosing why a cheap listing is not selling to a quality-seeking audience.

cards.title: Harness Social Proof to Lower Purchase Risk
cards.summary: When shoppers are uncertain, they copy the behavior of others, so showing credible peer evidence at the decision point reduces perceived risk and lifts conversion.
cards.use_when: Building PDP social-proof modules, category landing pages, cart abandonment messaging or new-product launches where buyer uncertainty is high.

cards.title: Use the Foot-in-the-Door for Micro-Commitments
cards.summary: A small, easy initial commitment changes a shopper's self-image and makes a larger related request more likely to be accepted—sequence matters.
cards.use_when: Designing onboarding flows, sampling-to-purchase paths, subscription upgrades, loyalty enrollment or progressive profiling where you want a large action after a small one.

cards.title: Use Rejection-Then-Retreat for Larger Requests
cards.summary: Making an oversized first request and, when refused, retreating to your actual (smaller) ask makes the target feel the second ask is a concession they should match.
cards.use_when: Structuring an upsell, a donation or tip request, a higher-tier offer, or a subscription-vs-one-time choice where you want to anchor high and still land a lower commitment.

cards.title:
Design Order Pages Around a Single
 high-ticket anchor
cards.summary: Sequencing and anchor design in the cart and PDP follow the contrast principle: put the large commitment first, then add-ons, and keep add-ons presented one at a time.
cards.use_when: Configuring the cart, checkout upsell slots, 'recommended items' carousels and threshold messaging so that add-ons benefit from an anchor rather than fight it.

cards.title: Set Up 'Setup' Options to Make the Preferred Choice Attractive
cards.summary: Presenting an undesirable option before the one you want sold, or showing an inflated reference first, uses contrast to make the target look better—useful in merchandising comparisons.
cards.use_when: Merchandising comparison pages, 'pairs well with' modules, plan/tier comparisons, or when a mid-priced item needs to look like the obvious value choice.

cards.title: Diagnose Buying Shortcuts Shoppers Actually Use
cards.summary: Shoppers lean on a few trigger features (price, popularity, authority, brand) when they lack the time or expertise to evaluate properly; identify the shortcut your category triggers and feed it credibly.
cards.use_when: Category strategy, PDP content priorities, and landing-page design when you must decide which single signal (price tier, review count, expert endorsement) to lead with.

cards.title: Protect Buyers Against Undiscovered Manipulation by Naming It
cards.summary: The source warns that trigger features can be mimicked to dupe buyers—so stores should both avoid deceptive mimicry and help customers recognize it, and auditors should test for it.
cards.use_when: Trust, compliance and merchandising review: auditing your own storefront for manipulative patterns, and training staff to spot deceptive 'mimicry' tactics used against your customers.

cards.title: Use Time/Stock Scarcity as a Signaling Device
cards.summary: Framing an offer as limited (by time or quantity) raises perceived value and urgency, and stores should use real limits rather than manufactured ones.
cards.use_when: Planning promotional messaging, drop or launch campaigns, cart timers, and low-stock badges across PDP and landing pages.

cards.title: Use Authority Cues to Reduce Decision Risk
cards.summary: Signals of legitimate authority (expertise, credentials, endorsements) reduce buyer uncertainty, and stores should present verifiable credentials rather than fabricated ones.
cards.use_when: PDP copy, ingredient or spec documentation, medical/technical product pages, and press or expert endorsement placement.

cards.title: Lean on Liking and Familiarity to Open Buying Relationships
cards.summary: Buyers say yes more easily to requesters they like or resemble, so stores can build affinity through their people, story and shared traits—without faking it.
cards.use_when: Brand storytelling, founder/team pages, creator partnerships, and community building where you want to lower a skeptical buyer's guard.

cards.title: Recognize That Repayment Obligation Can Outlast Its Usefulness
cards.summary: The source notes that reciprocal tactics eventually lose effectiveness as buyers learn to resist them—so retention should not depend on any single influence lever.
cards.use_when: Retention strategy, win-back programs and loyalty design: when deciding how much of your repeat-purchase engine should rest on gifting or obligation tactics versus product and service quality.

cards.title: Write Copy That Supplies the Shortcut, Not Just the Rationale
cards.summary: Shoppers respond to trigger features—a word, a price cue, a reason word—so copy should embed the specific trigger your category uses rather than only listing features.
cards.use_when: Landing page and PDP copywriting, ad creative, and email subject lines where you need the first few words to trigger a fast decision.

cards.title: Apply Influence Levers Only After Baseline Mechanics Work
cards.summary: Psychological optimization is a growth layer to apply once core store mechanics function—sequencing persuasion tactics before fixing fundamentals wastes effort.
cards.use_when: Prioritization: deciding whether to invest in persuasion/CRO copywork or in fixing site speed, checkout friction, inventory and tracking first.

cards.title: Sequence Persuasion Tactics to Avoid Self-Defeat
cards.summary: Influence principles can work against you if sequenced wrong (cheap before expensive, fake before real), so plan ordering and honesty deliberately.
cards.use_when: Merchandising and funnel sequencing decisions: ordering recommendations, choosing which signal leads, and reviewing promotions for accidental negative framing.

cards.title: Gate a free sample so it reads as a gift, not a trial
cards.summary: Frame samples and freebies as gifts (unrequested, non-returnable) to trigger the reciprocity rule and lift purchase or donation conversion.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether and how to add a free sample, gift-with-purchase, or unsolicited freebie to a PDP, cart, sampling program, or acquisition offer.

cards.title: Free-sample tactics: self-serve cutting and leave-behind kits
cards.summary: Two formats of sampling — self-serve cut portions and home leave-behind kits — that let customers try before buying and generate orders.
cards.use_when: Designing an in-store or at-home sampling program, or adapting samples to a subscription or replenishment offer.

cards.title: Uninvited gifts create debt even when unwanted
cards.summary: Unrequested gifts, even ones the recipient dislikes or discards, trigger repayment pressure that raises response rates.
cards.use_when: Choosing whether to add unsolicited inserts, samples, or gifts to an acquisition mailing, unboxing, or retargeting campaign.

cards.title: Use rejection-then-retreat to make a smaller ask land
cards.summary: Make a large request first and retreat to the request you actually want; the retreat is read as a concession to reciprocate.
cards.use_when: Structuring an offer ladder, upsell, price negotiation, referral ask, or checkout offer so the real target request is framed as a concession.

cards.title: Perceptual contrast: show the expensive anchor first
cards.summary: Presenting a high-priced item before a lower one makes the lower price feel smaller, lifting the lower-priced sale — and sometimes the average sale.
cards.use_when: Ordering products on a pricing page, bundle ladder, PDP comparison, or in-store/assisted selling sequence.

cards.title: Small favors still get repaid — sometimes with much larger ones
cards.summary: The reciprocity obligation is uncomfortable enough that people often return more than they received, which is why small first favors can trigger large asks.
cards.use_when: Designing the size of a first free offer relative to the purchase or commitment you will later request.

cards.title: Stockpile favors before you need them
cards.summary: Accumulated favors create a reservoir of obligation you can call in later, as LBJ did with Congress and Carter lacked.
cards.use_when: Planning long-horizon relationship building with suppliers, creators, affiliates, partners, or platforms before you need a specific ask.

cards.title: Reciprocal concessions drive compromise and unequal returns
cards.summary: Reciprocating a concession — not just a favor — is the mechanism behind negotiation retreats, and it can produce returns far larger than the concession given.
cards.use_when: Structuring any multi-step offer, quote, or negotiation where you concede something first to invite a matching concession.
